rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Nutrient cycling — carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Nutrient cycling — carbon** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Nutrient cycling (biogeochemical cycling) returns matter from organisms to the environment and back. Cycles are **gaseous** (reservoir in the atmosphere — carbon, nitrogen) or **sedimentary** (reservoir in rocks and soil — phosphorus, sulphur). The nitrogen cycle is the one with named bacterial specialists; the carbon cycle is the one we are now disturbing; the phosphorus cycle has no gas phase at all.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Carbon: atmosphere ↔ photosynthesis/respiration; CO2 ~0.03–0.04% of air; largest reservoir = ocean; human addition = fossil fuels — the reservoirs in one line each.  ·  Trick 2: Nitrogen: N2 (78% of air) unusable directly → fixation (Rhizobium, cyanobacteria, lightning) → nitrification (NH3 → NO2− → NO3−) → assimilation → denitrification (Pseudomonas back to N2) — the five stations.

(3) Why is the phosphorus cycle slower and without a gas phase? (4) How does the carbon cycle link to global warming? (5) Define ammonification and nitrification…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Cycles return matter to life: gaseous reservoirs (C, N) make fast cycles, sedimentary ones (P) are slow. The nitrogen cycle runs on named bacteria — fixers, nitrifiers, denitrifiers. **Self-check:** can you place Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Rhizobium and Pseudomonas at the right steps?
